title: EXP-130 — Final Read-Only Mock Application Study and Rebuild Specification
objective: Conduct one final, strictly read-only investigation of the existing Mock application using the current authenticated account. First inspect MockInventory's IDO metadata through the EXP-128 T27-supported exact-name runtime IDOs query. Then inspect the outstanding collection, Form-variable, and global Script inventory details through supported Designer interfaces. Perform one operator-assisted MockLoginPortal runtime observation, stopping before credentials are entered and resuming only after the operator independently completes the test login. Finally synthesize EXP-128 and EXP-130 evidence into a rebuild specification covering Forms, components, collections, scripts, variables, event handlers, IDOs, tables, assets, navigation, and runtime behavior, with proposed FX_-prefixed names for later creation in the operator's own account. No Mongoose artifact of any prefix may be created, modified, saved, or deleted in the current account.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md in full, including the 2026-10-25 read-only scope extension, before any browser interaction. Review the authoritative EXP-128 and EXP-129 records, relevant EXP-128 evidence, operator decisions, and applicable read-only procedures.

Use at most five bounded worker tasks: T1 MockInventory IDO inspection; T2 Designer metadata gaps; T3 pre-login runtime checkpoint; T4 post-operator-login observation; T5 repository-only synthesis and final audit.

T1: Confirm the inherited signed-in Web Client is usable and inspect the current runtime IDOs Form without changing its records. Confirm that IDO Name is empty, one blank row is shown, and no unsaved state or blocking prompt exists before the query.

T1: Apply the EXP-128 T27 procedure exactly: do not activate Filter in Place; select the IDO Name criterion, enter the literal MockInventory, and issue exactly one F4. If the prerequisite state differs, stop without typing or issuing F4.

T1: If exactly one MockInventory definition is returned, record the visible IDO identity and inspect its Tables, Properties, and Methods tabs without editing. Capture the base table, aliases, property identities, types, bindings, key-related attributes, method names, and relevant visible configuration only to the extent actually exposed.

T1: Transcribe the safely accessible MockInventory definition to evidence/EXP-130/MockInventory-ido-definition.txt. Include source identity, tab names, source-to-evidence mapping, and explicit completeness limitations. Follow the format of EXP-128's MockLogin definition copy only if that copy is confirmed in the authoritative record.
T1: Close the runtime IDOs Form using its ordinary non-saving close path. Answer No to any save prompt. Do not execute Methods, navigate to data records, or inspect unrelated IDOs.

T2: Open only the existing MockInventory and MockInventoryDashboard definitions required for the named design-time questions. Confirm each actual Form name and loaded version identity from the supported UI rather than relying solely on captions or recent-form labels.

T2: Inspect collection Options and Filter settings for MockInventory and MockInventoryDashboard, corresponding to EXP-128 Q-11. Record collection identity, IDO binding, visible Options, filter expressions, and any collection-level settings relevant to the later rebuild.

T2: Inspect the existing definitions of vInventoryJson and vMockLoginJson through the Forms' Variables interfaces and the supported Designer Edit > Variable interface, corresponding to EXP-128 Q-4 and Q-5.

T2: For each variable, record whether it is actually present on each inspected surface and, if exposed, its category, persistence setting, Global setting, initial value, and owning Form or scope. Do not infer an absent variable's definition from a component binding or script reference.

T2: Inspect only the previously skipped segment of the Designer Edit > Script global Scripts inventory between GetChartTypeByChartStyle and GetDataLakeObjects, as identified by EXP-128 T21. Record displayed Script names and coverage boundaries only; do not open their source editors.

T2: Dismiss every inspection dialog with Cancel or the supported non-saving close control. Close only Forms opened by this experiment, without saving. Preserve all previously open Forms and their state.

T3: Open the existing MockLoginPortal once through the supported Web Client Form-opening workflow. Capture exactly one screenshot of the empty login card showing the Form identity and visible controls without any entered credentials.

T3: End the worker task immediately after the empty-login screenshot and a short checkpoint report. The coordinator must pause for explicit operator action. Do not submit a follow-up browser instruction before the operator has completed the login and authorized observation.

Operator-only checkpoint: The operator independently enters the Mock test credentials and activates Sign in. No worker observes, types, records, transcribes, or screenshots credential entry. The operator supplies a completion signal without revealing credentials.

T4: After the operator's completion signal, inspect only the resulting rendered application state. Record any visible messages, whether navigation occurred, the identity of any automatically opened Form, and the login-to-dashboard transition relevant to EXP-128 Q-3.

T4: Record the dashboard's rendered structure, labels, navigation elements, charts, summary indicators, and other non-sensitive UI elements needed for reconstruction. Do not select records, expand data rows, activate buttons, or click within Mock application Forms.

T4: Capture only credential-free and non-sensitive post-login screenshots. Redact sensitive information before writing evidence. If credentials remain visible or cannot be reliably excluded, do not capture the affected surface.
T4: Close only runtime Forms opened by the worker during EXP-130, using ordinary non-saving closure and No for any save prompt. Do not close inherited pre-existing Forms.
T5: Review the completed EXP-128 and EXP-130 evidence and produce a REBUILD SPECIFICATION in the EXP-130 experiment record. This is a documentation-only task with no browser interaction.

T5: Inventory every identified Mock Form, component, collection, script, variable, event handler, IDO, SQL table, asset, and navigation dependency required for reconstruction. Include exact source identities where proven, proposed FX_-prefixed destination identities, relevant attributes, dependency relationships, and evidence references.
T5: Provide a readiness checklist for each required rebuild element using known, partly known, or unknown. Unknown details must remain unresolved rather than filled with assumptions.
T5: Provide a dependency-ordered reproduction plan for the operator's own account. Clearly label all proposed creations, configuration steps, and runtime tests as not executed and unverified.
T5: Produce a concise acceptance matrix, browser-action accounting, evidence manifest, limitations summary, and repository-confinement audit.
Write repository content only to the EXP-130 experiment record and evidence/EXP-130/. Existing files and prior experiment records are read-only.
Apply EXP-128's credential redaction, console-count stop rule, no-browser-JavaScript rule, and non-saving dismissal procedures throughout.

Allow at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection for browser recovery. If the issue remains unresolved, stop that inspection and record a blocker without widening scope.

Inspecting, exporting, or opening Mock application data records.
Reading MockLogin Password values or any other authentication credential.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence under evidence/EXP-130/ establishes the usable inherited signed-in session, User editing scope for Designer inspections, clean Designer state, console baseline, and repository baseline. No Mongoose mutation is performed. The inherited FX_InventoryPrototype01 remains untouched.

The runtime IDOs query evidence shows the prerequisite empty IDO Name field and blank row, followed by exactly one MockInventory criterion and one F4. No Filter in Place activation occurs. A returned target must be identified visibly by its exact IDO Name. If the result is absent or ambiguous, record the lookup as blocked rather than claiming that the definition was recovered.

If the exact MockInventory definition is located, evidence identifies the Tables, Properties, and Methods tabs and their visible contents. evidence/EXP-130/MockInventory-ido-definition.txt contains a source-attributed transcription of the accessible metadata, with an explicit list of unavailable or unverified fields. No IDO method or data-record operation occurs.

Evidence captures the exact loaded MockInventory and MockInventoryDashboard design-time Form identities and their collection Options and filter settings, or explicitly identifies which settings cannot be exposed through the permitted UI. The worker makes no changes and dismisses the inspection surfaces without saving.

Evidence records the observed presence or absence of vInventoryJson and vMockLoginJson in the inspected Forms' Variables surfaces and Edit > Variable. For each located definition, the displayed category, persistence, Global setting, initial value, and scope are recorded where visible. Any unresolved definition is marked unknown rather than inferred.

A bounded, names-only inventory captures the previously skipped global Script segment between GetChartTypeByChartStyle and GetDataLakeObjects. The evidence identifies the visible coverage boundaries and listed names. No Script source is opened and no global Script is edited.

The pre-login checkpoint consists of exactly one credential-free screenshot of the empty MockLoginPortal login card, with visible Form identification, followed by termination of the worker task. The record explicitly states that no login was attempted by the worker and that operator action is pending. No filled-login screenshot exists in EXP-130 evidence.

Following an explicit operator completion signal, the next worker task captures the resulting credential-free UI state, any visible messages, observed navigation, opened Form identity, and dashboard layout. Evidence distinguishes directly observed behavior from EXP-128 hypotheses. No worker click occurs within the Mock Forms. If the login fails or the resulting state cannot be safely observed, that actual result is recorded without further login attempts.

A final application-state audit confirms that inspection dialogs are dismissed, only worker-opened Forms have been closed, any save prompts received No, the Designer has no unsaved changes attributable to this run, and no prohibited Mongoose mutation is observed. Console counts and browser-action logs are reconciled with the EXP-128 stop rule.

The EXP-130 record contains a source-attributed REBUILD SPECIFICATION covering each identified Mock Form, component, collection, asset, script, variable, handler, IDO, table, and navigation dependency. Every proposed replacement identity begins with FX_. Missing source details are explicitly marked unknown; no proposed identity is represented as an already existing artifact.

A readiness checklist assigns known, partly known, or unknown to every required rebuild element and cites the evidence supporting its classification. A dependency-ordered reproduction plan identifies what should later be created and tested in the operator's own account. The entire plan is explicitly classified unverified and unexecuted.

The final evidence manifest, task summaries, and action-accounting report are written under evidence/EXP-130/ with short, explicit proof statements and limitations. The repository audit establishes that run-attributable writes are confined to the EXP-130 experiment record and evidence directory, subject to authoritative operator Git review. No existing recipe or prior experiment record is changed.

initial_instruction: EXP-130 T1 ONLY — READ-ONLY MOCKINVENTORY IDO DEFINITION. This proposal requires operator approval before execution. First read AGENTS.md completely, including its 2026-10-25 read-only scope extension. Review the authoritative EXP-128 record, especially T27 and any confirmed later MockLogin definition transcription, and EXP-129's preservation requirements. Capture the current authenticated session, applicable scope, clean-state baseline, console counts, and repository baseline. Do not interact with FX_InventoryPrototype01. Open the supported runtime IDOs Form and verify the precise prerequisite state: empty IDO Name, one blank row, and no pending change or prompt. If this state differs, stop before entering a criterion. Do not activate Filter in Place. Select the IDO Name criterion, enter exactly MockInventory, and issue exactly ONE F4. Capture the exact returned identity and row cardinality. If exactly one matching definition is visibly established, inspect only its Tables, Properties, and Methods tabs without changing any value, executing a Method, or opening records. Transcribe the accessible metadata into evidence/EXP-130/MockInventory-ido-definition.txt with source identity, tab-level references, and completeness limitations. If the lookup or any tab inspection is blocked, record that limitation without retrying the query or widening the search. Close only the runtime IDOs Form opened for T1, using ordinary non-saving closure and No if prompted. Apply EXP-128 credential redaction, console-count stop conditions, and the single-snapshot/single-corrected-inspection recovery budget. Write a concise T1 result with evidence paths, acceptance-check status, and action counts. Stop after T1. Do not begin Designer variable inspection, global Script inventory inspection, MockLoginPortal runtime observation, operator login, or rebuild synthesis. Wait for separate coordinator authorization for T2.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261025-180517-kdWc. Rationale: EXP-128 established substantial observational knowledge of the Mock application but left several important gaps: the MockInventory IDO definition, collection Options and filters, variable definitions, part of the global Script inventory, and the actual login-to-dashboard transition. EXP-129 successfully demonstrated isolated FX_ Form creation, but its FX_InventoryPrototype01 was created in the Mock application's account and must remain untouched. The operator has designated this account exclusively for read-only learning. EXP-130 will consolidate the remaining observations into an evidence-grounded rebuild specification for a different account. Unlike earlier creation experiments, this study intentionally has no Mongoose Save or mutation lifecycle. Its verification consists of read-only inspection, safe dismissal of inspection surfaces, controlled operator-assisted runtime observation, and a final non-mutation audit. It does not replay EXP-128 or promote any candidate technique to replay_verified.
